data.why: The repository bundles a pre-computed demo snapshot (demo/processed/*.parquet and *.json) from the public GoldenCheetah OpenData cohort; the dashboard auto-detects that data/processed is empty (it is .gitignored and never populated in a fresh checkout) and transparently switches to the demo snapshot, so no uploads or synthetic files are needed.

goals: Inspect how training load (TRIMP-derived fitness/fatigue curves) tracks acute:chronic workload ratio for the demo athlete on the Charge page
Check whether a rolling performance envelope is more predictable than raw per-session effort on the Performance page
Compare dose-response model variants (persistence, mean, Banister, load model) in and out of sample on the Diagnostics page
Review whether the per-athlete load effect replicates across the 61-athlete cohort, and how many athletes show a confidence interval excluding zero
Examine the hierarchical Bayesian pooling of time constants across athletes and the window-sensitivity control analysis
Check which planner safety rules (e.g. ACWR >= 0.8) are validated against real outcome data on the Mesures > Regles du plan tab

review.summary: The tree follows the dashboard faithfully from one athlete's load and envelope to cohort replication, pooling and rule validation, and every screen I sampled supports its node. It misses the README's central finding that load must match the target's discipline, files the readiness ladder in the wrong phase, and has no features for several reusable components (detectability floor, predictor screen, readiness checklist, metric cross-check), so it needs fixes before filing.
